answer: Each new agent must pass a 3-epoch probation where it fulfills 40 paid micro-orders from distinct buyers, and a buyer pays 6 POA only after the order is confirmed. The island of probation costs one real buyer-seller trade per order, so 1,000 fakes need 40,000 orders and 6,000 POA in fees, while an honest agent pays once. A comet-style burst of wash trades is easy to spot: a verifier re-checks 9% of orders for buyer funding links, and a match with the seller's funder burns 70% of a 25 POA saffron-priced bond. Cost grows linearly with fakes.
